Attempts to reach Dexter King for comment were unsuccessful. However, a source close to the estate, who spoke on condition of anonymity, characterized the lawsuit as "deeply disappointing" and suggested the matter could have been resolved privately within the family.

## Legacy Under Scrutiny

Legal experts say the case highlights the complexities that can arise when families attempt to manage the commercial legacy of a historical figure alongside personal grief and differing visions for how that legacy should be honored.

"These kinds of disputes are unfortunately common when you have valuable intellectual property tied to a beloved public figure," said one Atlanta-based estate attorney not connected to the case. "The emotional stakes are just as high as the financial ones, which makes these family conflicts particularly painful and public."

The King Center, located along Auburn Avenue in Atlanta near Dr. King's birth home and the Ebenezer Baptist Church where he once preached, remains a significant tourist destination and continues to operate independently of the lawsuit, according to center officials.

No court date has yet been set for the proceedings. Legal analysts suggest the case could take months to resolve, particularly if it proceeds to a full accounting and potential trial rather than a private settlement.

CNN has reached out to representatives for both Bernice King and Martin Luther King III, as well as Dexter King, for further comment on this developing story.
